title: "Know Your Gear"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Three Kinds of Machine. **Objective:** use the eight words this site relies on (model, harness, skill, MCP, hook, plugin, effort, eval) and say how they fit together.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code and API docs on 2026-11-16 (sources in `research/terminology.md`). Other tools name things differently; the ideas carry over.</span>
:::

People mix these words up, and the mix-ups cause real mistakes, such as blaming "the model" for something a setting did. In this world the **companions are models**, and the **harness is their armour**.

## The words

- **Model.** The LLM that reads and writes text (for example Claude Sonnet 5.5, or a local model through Ollama). It is not the product you type into. Aliases such as `sonnet` move to newer versions over time, so pin the full name when a result must be reproducible.
- **Harness.** The program around the model. Per the Claude Code docs it provides the tools, manages the context the model sees, runs the loop (gather context, act, check, repeat) and enforces permissions. Claude Code and OpenCode are harnesses. Many questions are really about the harness: what may it touch, what does it remember, what does it ask first?
- **Skill.** A folder with a `SKILL.md`. Only its short description is preloaded; the body loads when it is used. It advises. (You wrote one in Forge a Skill, later in this world.)
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol).** An open standard for connecting the harness to outside tools and data, such as a database or a literature search. A server you connect can act on your behalf, so treat it like software you install.
- **Hook.** Your own command, request or prompt that the harness runs automatically at a set point, such as before a tool call. A command hook that exits with code 2 stops the action whatever the model wants. A rule in an instructions file can only ask. That is why hooks are the stronger guard.
- **Plugin.** A folder that bundles skills, hooks, MCP servers and more, installed as one unit. It can run code, so it is a trust decision.
- **Effort.** A setting for how much the model reasons per step, from `low` to `max` in Claude Code (`/effort`, `--effort`). Low is faster and cheaper; high thinks longer and checks more. It is a behavioural signal, not an exact budget. The docs warn that `max` can show diminishing returns and overthink, so raise it only where you measure a gain. It makes answers more careful, not guaranteed correct.
- **Eval.** A repeatable test of agent behaviour: a prompt plus checks on the result. Comparing runs **with** and **without** something (a skill, a rule) shows what it contributed. A score of 100% both ways means it contributed nothing.

::: {.callout-note}
Naming differs between tools. The Claude Code docs define "harness" and "hooks" as above; do not assume another tool's hooks, plugins or effort settings work the same way. Check its docs.
:::
